summary: Configured persistent name-based Apache sites on node1:8080. Both approved content trees are served correctly, unknown hosts receive HTTP 403, and the configuration survived a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-native Apache 2.4 packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test as separate virtual hosts sharing TCP 8080.
Configured the default virtual host to deny unknown Host headers.
Added persistent SELinux and firewalld rules for Apache on TCP 8080.
Enabled Apache at boot and preserved the staged content.
Restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all sites recovered.

evidence.requirement: docs.branch.test serves the supplied docs tree on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: Apache listens on 8080; the docs index and handbook returned HTTP 200 with matching source checksums, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: orders.branch.test serves the supplied orders tree on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: The orders index and catalog returned HTTP 200 with matching source checksums, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Unknown Host headers receive an error and tenants remain isolated
evidence.summary: Unknown hosts returned HTTP 403 before and after restart; cross-tenant file probes returned HTTP 404.
The supplied docs and orders file SHA-256 checksums remained unchanged through configuration and restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 remained unchanged; Apache 2.4.62 was installed from the configured RHEL 9 repositories.

Healthy baseline boot ID 5f3ce3b8-4860-447e-bcf1-d6643718694e was captured, reboot was acknowledged, new boot ID a27261f5-bccd-443b-b1c0-cccf6c49e436 was observed, and Apache, port 8080, firewall access, both content trees, and unknown-host denial recovered.
